title: Exercise‐related sudden cardiac death of an American football player with arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia/cardiomyopathy AND sarcoidosis
case_prompt: A 28‐year‐old male American football player (176 cm, 105 kg) presented after two episodes of exercise‐related syncope associated with palpitations during intensive physical activity. Family history was negative for sudden cardiac death or early cardiac disease. Clinical examination, blood tests, and 12‐lead ECG were unremarkable, with no ε waves, T‐wave inversions, or delayed terminal activation. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed right ventricular enlargement without dyskinesia. Exercise testing and signal‐averaged ECG showed no pathological findings. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a severely dilated right ventricle (end‐diastolic volume/BSA = 130 mL/m2) with bulging, pronounced regional dyssynchrony, and moderately decreased right ventricular systolic function (ejection fraction = 42%). Cardiac MRI fulfilled one major criterion for ARVD/C. A myocardial biopsy was refused by the patient. Genetic testing was scheduled, and he was strongly advised to discontinue intensive exercise.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. ARVD/C was supported by cardiac MRI findings fulfilling a major diagnostic criterion — “Cardiac MRI fulfilled one major criterion for ARVD/C.”  
2. Cardiac sarcoidosis was considered as a differential because of overlapping diagnostic criteria — “As 2010 diagnostic criteria for ARVD/C have limited discrimination between cardiac sarcoidosis and ARVD/C, cardiac sarcoidosis is an important differential diagnosis.”  
3. Cardiac sarcoidosis was excluded by the absence of cardiac granulomas at autopsy — “There was no evidence of cardiac involvement of sarcoidosis.”
